name: spaces_create_node
description: Create nodes. ~10 per call is the sweet spot; 20 is the hard maximum. Each item: nodeType + semantic data. @see guides_get('spaces')

data.description: Node data: prompt, script, instructions, aspectRatio, model; panel: name/color; creation node: pass the creation `identifier` as `creationIdentifier`. Branded image-generator: data.prompt = topic + hard constraints, never the template name (brandKitTemplateSlug + chip carry it); data.mode = magnific-one (Brand Kit only works with it; a run with another model is switched to it).

layout.description: Where the node goes, declared by relations: groupId (panel it belongs to; a panel inside another panel is accepted only for accounts with nested groups enabled, up to 6 levels including the root, and otherwise lands at top level with the reason in placementReason) and relativeToNodeId + direction (left/right/above/below), optional alignment (start/center/end, default start), optional inheritPanel (default true). Both accept an existing node id OR the `ref` of an earlier item in this same call. x/y are a preferred spot only: the board moves the node if it collides (relocated[]). width/height are ignored — size follows node type (a creation node takes the ratio of its media) — except on panel (200x150 to 20000) and sticky-note (216 to 5000), which keep the size given (e.g. a 3816x150 panel as a block header); a panel with members is refit around them when they change, which overrides that size. Omit layout to let the backend space nodes out.

nodeType.description: Node type slug; spaces_node_types_search explains each one.

prompt.description: Node prompt/brief. No workflow instructions. Branded image-generator: short topic + user constraints only; kit/template own look; never the template name or slug (it rides on data.brandKitTemplateSlug and the canvas shows it as a chip). Never empty when a Brand Kit is attached.

ref.description: Short alias for this node (letters, digits, _ or -), usable by LATER items of this same call in layout.relativeToNodeId / layout.groupId. Node ids only exist after the call returns, so this is the only way to chain or group nodes created together.
